column1: Hettie|There you are, love. I can spare a moment if the hens can.
Gwil|Mind the shavings, Corin. What have you got on your mind?
Odo|Quiet feet, lad. The fish needn't hear the whole conversation.
Tolan|Keep your voice down. I can hear you without the whole patrol hearing too.
Serjeant Bram|Stand properly when you address me, boy. Now, what is it?
Doran|You've found a knight with a moment to spare. Don't make me regret it.
Elder Maddock|Come, Corin. A question is easier to carry once you've spoken it.
Pip|I felt your footsteps coming! What made you stop here?
Mycella|Tread gently, young one. There is time enough to listen.
Bolete|A moment's company would be welcome. The roots can wait.
Truffle|Careful of the little caps. Come closer; there's room beside them.
The Shroom King|You may speak beneath this crown. You needn't bow to be heard.
Calder|Rest your feet a moment. The road will still be there when we're done.
Prue|Hello, Corin. It's good to rest my hands and use my voice for a change.
Toft|Come to talk? Good. I've heard enough echoes for one day.
Linna|Corin! Have you brought news, or shall we compare what we've heard?
Wren|Something troubling you, or just stopping for a chat? Either is welcome.
Bevan|Mind the apples with your elbows, and we'll get along splendidly.
Isolde|A familiar face improves the day. What shall we talk about, Corin?
Nazim|Welcome. A little shade and a little conversation cost nothing here.
Halima|Come closer. The wind carries enough gossip without our help.
Tarek|If you're looking for agreeable company, try me before the camel.
Suhaila|Let me finish this stitch. There, now you have my attention.
Idris|Tell me, traveler: have you come with a question or a good story?
Rashida|Hello there. Keep your sleeves clear of the glass and stay a while.
Bilal|You look less likely to climb my roof than the goats. Welcome.
Sella|There's always time to talk while a pot gathers its flavor.
Ovid|Speak up a little. My ears are still keeping time with the hammers.
Jamila|A customer or a conversation? I'm pleased to see either.
Nerissa|You have the look of someone who's been farther than the shallows.
Astrid|Come and catch your breath. Nobody tells a good story while shivering.
Colm|Stay a moment, Corin. A meal is better when there's someone to talk to.
Tessa|Hello! Have you a request, or may I rest my fingers and listen?
Rowan the Hunter|Well met, Corin. I hope the road's been kinder to you than my boots.
Sverre|Good to see you upright and out of the weather. What's on your mind?
Runa|You're welcome to talk, so long as you don't mind me keeping an eye on supper.
Eira|Corin! A chat goes down nicely with a little cider.
Fenton|A visitor! Splendid. I was running out of people to tell my stories to.
Tallis|Give me a moment to let that tune out of my head. There. Hello.
Kip|Did you find anything interesting? Even something small counts.
Ada|Come in, Corin. If Rowan sent you with an excuse, I shall know.
Bren|Have you heard a good story? I like knowing where the telling began.
Berta|Now then, Corin. What needs tending: a scrape, a worry, or your curiosity?
Della|Hello, dear. There's usually more to a person than the neighbors say.
Ewan|Ah, company. I can put the book aside for a question worth asking.
Fara|Mind your step. I'd rather welcome you than sweep up after you.
Garrick|Corin. Stay a while; I could use a voice that doesn't sound like a hammer.
Hester|I can mend and listen at the same time. Go on, then.
Junia|Good to see you. Sit a moment while I finish saving this old thing.
Kellan|Hello! You're just in time, though I couldn't tell you what for.
Lysa|Come and talk, Corin. It's nice to admire something with company.
Cinder|A welcome face. There's warmth enough here for a little conversation.
Warden|I thought I heard someone coming. What brings you to my doorstep?
Ember|Brush the dust from your coat, then tell me how you're getting on.
Dagna|Please tell me those boots are cleaner than they look. Hello, Corin.
Lode|Come closer. The forge has been trying to have this conversation for us.
Pike|Hello, love. Have you been remembering to stop for your meals?
Hallow|If you've come about the hinge, it has survived another day. What else is new?
Quarrel|Come to hear a complaint? I have several, and a few pleasantries besides.
Flint|Stay out of the draft, Corin. We can talk while the fire settles.
Winnie|Look at you, Corin. Come and tell an old friend of Nan's how you are.
Ned|Let me set this buckle down. Right, lad. I'm listening.
Nan Ferrow|Come here, love. There's always time for you.
Joss|Hello, Corin. A visit's a fine excuse to leave the chores for a moment.
Osric|A visitor with both boots on the ground. That's how the best adventures start.
Alder|Slowly does it, Corin. The bees and I both prefer an unhurried visit.
Gwyneth|Mind the wool. I've left room for company, though the scarf disagrees.
Bors|Hello there. If you've brought half the road on your boots, leave it outside.
Kiln|Welcome. Questions are less fragile than bowls, so ask away.
Petra|Good day, Corin. What have you heard along the road?
Raff|Stay on the shady side, lad. We'll both think more clearly there.
Suri|A loose strap or a friendly word? I can help with either.
Tavin|Hello! Come clear of the doorway so we don't become part of the furniture.
Una|Corin, how lovely. Let me put this parcel aside and hear your news.
Vela|Welcome. You can look at the weaving while we talk; I won't charge for looking.
Wystan|A moment, Corin. Let me finish counting before conversation makes me generous.
Rania|Come and rest your feet. There's no prize for standing in this heat.
Latif|Hello, young traveler. A little conversation might improve my arithmetic.
Yara|Mind the latch. The sea has been arguing with it again.
Doryn|Well met. What are the roads saying? The gulls have had their turn.
Bry|Watch that step, Corin. I'd like this visit to begin without a splash.
Coral|Hello, dear. Have you come from the water, or from farther inland?
Edda|Come under a sound roof for a moment. How has the road treated you?
Fennel|Oh, it's you. Shut the door behind you, and we can have a proper chat.
Bjorn|Welcome, Corin. There's room by the warmth if you'd like to stay a little.
Cap|Keep to the firmer ground, friend. The moss is resting.
Ilsa|Hello, traveler. Careful where you stand; those shoots are still growing.
Meriel|Welcome! Take your time looking. Sela's glass rewards a second glance.
Elin|Oh, hello. I was trying to choose a favorite, and making very little progress.
Maelis|You've come this far, boy. You might as well say what you want.
Archivist Elowen|Welcome, Corin. Bring your questions; we'll see which ones the shelves can answer.
Mira|Hello. Have you brought an account from the road, or come looking for one?
Oren|Come and sit with a question, Corin. Even difficult subjects deserve company.
Tamsin|You can talk to me here. The quiet needn't mean we all sit alone.
Master Iven|Ah, Corin. What has the world been teaching you lately?
Brin|Come and look, Corin. Another pair of eyes might make sense of these drawings.
Nell|Keep your voice comfortable, Corin. Some subjects make the room listen back.
Sable|Hello. Have you found something the books disagree about? I usually do.
Pella|Come over, Corin. I was just wondering what it's like beyond the edge of a map.
Bess|Welcome to the Copper Cup. Settle your feet, and tell me what you need.
Ronan|Hello there. If you're here for a chat, I promise not to talk only about cider.
Venn|Corin! You look as though you might have news worth carrying.
Hobb|Ah, company. This table has heard my thoughts often enough already.
Edric|Well met, fellow traveler. Taking a rest, or planning the next stretch?
Dorr|Hm? Oh, hello. I'm awake enough for a short conversation. Probably.
Ser Anwen|You're welcome to speak freely with me, Corin. Take your time.
Grusk|Pull your hands clear of the cards, then tell me what's on your mind.
Fen|Corin! A conversation will give my feet a well-earned rest.
Senn|Come to talk or test your luck? Best decide before Dain notices you.
Dain|A new face at the table! Let's see whether your news is worth a wager.
Rusk|Hello, lad. It's good to hear another voice after a long stretch of road.
Linnet|Oh, hello! You'll have to excuse me if that tune keeps sneaking back in.
Puck|Come for the music or the company? I'll try to be agreeable at both.
Vale|Mind the brim. There is a person under this hat, and he's pleased to see you.
Cerys|Hello, Corin. Have you come to ask a question or improve your excuses?
Nyra|You have my attention. Dain only thinks he has the rest of it.
Maren|Welcome, traveler. Take a breath; there's no hurry to explain yourself.
Dunstan|Keep clear of the hot work, Corin. Now, what can I do for you?
Sela|Hello, Corin. Give your eyes a moment; the glass catches every bit of light.
Tam|Corin! You've caught me between jobs. I won't tell if you don't.
Celia|Come and talk. A living voice is a pleasant change from copying old ones.
Ivo|Hello there. I was just putting a few things in order. What's new with you?
Merrin|I saw you coming, Corin. It's good when someone stops instead of passing by.
Zella|Mind the loose cord, love. Sit where I can see you while I mend.
Iris|Close the cold out behind you, Corin, and tell me how you've been.
Alderic|You have reached a place with a long memory. What would you ask of it?
King Halvard|Speak, boy. Being granted my attention does not entitle you to waste it.
Cartwright Oswin|Mind the wheel, lad. I can spare a word more easily than a sound axle.
Miner Marn|Keep your feet on firm ground, Corin. What brings you this way?
Miner Nerik|Hello! If Marn asks, we're discussing something useful.
Snowbuilder Nessa|Come and see, Corin. I think a little company improves the cold.
Orin|There's room to pause here. Tell me how the day's treating you.
Weft|Hello, Corin. A patient word is welcome while I untangle this.
Dorrick|Come to talk? Good. Work has had enough of my attention for now.
Hask|An ordinary visit, I hope? Those are my favorite sort.
Garrow|Let me put these tools down. Right. What can I do for you, lad?
Marek|You have time for a chat, I hope. I dislike hurrying the pleasant parts of a day.
Bregga|Come closer, Corin. Best have our talk before the weather changes its mind.
Torvald|Welcome, lad. A clear light and good company improve most things.
Ingrid|The latch is settled and so am I. Tell me what's on your mind.
Sigrun|Hello, Corin. You look as though a dry place and a kind word wouldn't hurt.
Asta|You've found me comfortable, Corin. A conversation would finish the arrangement.
Aurelius|I am listening, Corin. What shall we wonder about together?
Edwin|Morning, Corin. The hens can manage without my supervision for a moment.
